title: Avocado: Ancient Avocado Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: Grown for fruit almost everywhere, for shade almost nowhere. Barcelona's avocado at Placa de Can Bruixa has climbed to 17 metres since 1945.
intro: Persea americana is native to central Mexico and grown almost everywhere in Europe for its fruit rather than its shade, which makes a mature specimen remarkable rather than ordinary. It wants heat, water and no frost, and a tree grown from a stone takes a decade or more to fruit and then usually disappoints whoever planted it. Barcelona has catalogued two for their size instead. The one on Placa de Can Bruixa in Les Corts went into the ground in 1945 and, unpruned for picking, simply went up: 17 metres on a trunk only 80 centimetres round. The other stands in front of the Teatre Lliure, planted around 1946 beside a building that has been an exposition pavilion, a flower market and finally a theatre, with a canopy 15 metres across. Nobody has recorded whether it still fruits.
